newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close mostly higher, yen down.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close mostly higher, yen down.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mostly higher, with December marks and Swiss francs wrapping up a lackluster afternoon on the top side of their intraday ranges, traders and analysts said.
Both contracts established their ranges early in the session after finding follow-through buying from overnight trade.
One analyst said several speculative accounts were heavy buyers of cash mark/yen, slightly firming the mark/yen cross.
Cash yen's continued declines against most currencies helped keep yen futures on the defensive.
December yen tested its contract low at $0.008926, which was set on GLOBEX, but bounced off that area in thin pit volume, traders said.
They are still targeting the $0.8917 level, or 113.00 spot yen, as the next support level. Further support rests at $0.008879 or 113.50 spot.

Traders and analysts said the Japanese Liberal Democratic Party's showing in the general elections had marginal affect on the yen, merely cementing beliefs that the Japanese interest rates would stay low.

Canadian dollar futures sustained gains, despite talk in the cash markets that the Bank of Canada may yet again lower interest rates due to the strength of the cash Canadian dollar and after a retail sales report came out weak.
December Canadian dollars rose to $0.7451 after dipping below support at $0.7425 at the opening.
December's contract high is at $0.7460, which was set on October 5, 1995. On a continuation chart, Canadian dollar futures rose to $0.7466, which is equivalent to 1.3428 spot.
Sterling remained higher on options-related buying. One analyst said one major bank was a heavy buyer of sterling calls in the cash market.
December sterling remained below its overnight high of $1.5950 set.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was down $0.000020 at $0.008937, marks were up $0.0032 at $0.6538, Swiss francs were $0.0044 higher at $0.7961, sterling was up $0.0030 at $1.5912, Canadian dollars rose $0.0008 at $0.7450, Australian dollars were $0.0019 higher at $0.7958 and Mexican pesos were down $0.000350 at $0.124475.
